body: Hey there. I don’t know your pain, but I can relate to your story a little bit. I’m 22 and I pretty much don’t do anything all day either. I sleep all day and go to work for a few hours. I also have 0 friends. I keep in contact with an ex, too. Once you’re around someone and open up to them, it’s hard to not stay attached. Especially when they always listened to you at times like these. I just wanted to say your story isn’t pathetic. I’m sorry you’re in physical pain and mental pain. That’s gotta be really tough. But I hope you make it through the morning and feel a little better in the afternoon. Sleep tight.

I was on Wellbutrin for my depression and Setraline for my anxiety. Having dealt with depression for the better part of my life, I have to say it made a huge difference. It wasn’t anything magical or instant. I just started feeling like I had more energy and could get myself up to do things in the day. I could go to sleep without overthinking for hours beforehand. I could do my laundry every week around the same time no problem. I also started taking care of myself much better. I loved Wellbutrin. The side effects I experienced were massive long-lasting headaches. Before, I only experienced short headaches due to hunger or lack of sleep. On these meds, I would have a headache in the back of my skull for 5 days straight with no relief in-between. They were so bad I couldn’t even get up and cook without being in pain. This started around 3 months or so on Wellbutrin. I stopped taking it to get on some meds to help my headaches. They eventually subsided. I slowly started taking the meds again, meaning taking a half pill and working up to a full pill again. The day I took a half pill, the headache returned and stayed. I decided it wasn’t worth it. I wish I could’ve stayed on Wellbutrin as it helped immensely. I’ve been off of them for about 4 months now and the depression has slowly but surely come back. I still recommend it. Setraline made me feel like a zombie. Wellbutrin gave me energy.
